title: Adult CPR

steps.title: Check for Safety
steps.text: Ensure the scene is safe for you and the victim. Put on gloves if available.

steps.title: Check Responsiveness
steps.text: Tap the person's shoulders firmly and shout 'Are you OK?'. Look for normal breathing.

steps.title: Call Emergency Services
steps.text: Call 911 (or your local emergency number). Ask a bystander to get an AED if available.

steps.title: Position the Person
steps.text: Place the person on their back on a firm, flat surface. Kneel beside them.

steps.title: Hand Position
steps.text: Place the heel of one hand on the centre of the chest (lower half of sternum). Place your other hand on top, fingers interlaced.

steps.title: Chest Compressions
steps.text: Push hard and fast — compress at least 5 cm (2 inches). Allow full chest recoil between compressions. Rate: 100–120 compressions/minute.

steps.title: Rescue Breaths (if trained)
steps.text: After 30 compressions, give 2 rescue breaths: tilt head, lift chin, pinch nose, seal mouth, breathe for 1 second each watching for chest rise.

steps.title: Continue 30:2 cycle
steps.text: Continue 30 compressions : 2 breaths until AED arrives, EMS takes over, or the person shows signs of life.

notes: If untrained or unwilling to give breaths, perform compression-only CPR continuously at 100–120/min until EMS arrives.

steps.title: Ensure Safety
steps.text: Check the scene is safe. Approach the child carefully.

steps.title: Check Responsiveness
steps.text: Tap the child's shoulder and shout their name. Check for breathing — no more than 10 seconds.

steps.title: Call for Help
steps.text: Send someone to call emergency services. If alone, perform 2 minutes of CPR first, then call.

steps.title: Open Airway
steps.text: Tilt head back gently, lift chin to open the airway.

steps.title: Give 2 Rescue Breaths
steps.text: Seal your mouth over the child's mouth and nose. Give 2 gentle breaths, 1 second each. Chest should rise visibly.

steps.title: Compressions
steps.text: Use 1–2 hands. Compress 1/3 depth of chest (~5 cm). 30 compressions at 100–120/min.

steps.title: Continue 30:2
steps.text: Alternate 30 compressions and 2 breaths until AED is available or EMS arrives.

steps.title: Assess Severity
steps.text: Ask 'Are you choking?' If they can cough, speak, or breathe — encourage coughing. Do NOT intervene yet.

steps.title: Severe — 5 Back Blows
steps.text: Stand beside and slightly behind them. Support chest with one hand. Give 5 firm back blows between shoulder blades with heel of your hand.

steps.title: Check After Each Blow
steps.text: Check if obstruction is cleared after each blow. Stop if object is expelled.

steps.title: 5 Abdominal Thrusts (Heimlich)
steps.text: Stand behind them, arms around waist. Place one fist (thumb side in) above navel, below ribcage. Grasp with other hand. Pull sharply inward and upward. Repeat up to 5 times.

steps.title: Alternate until clear
steps.text: Alternate 5 back blows and 5 abdominal thrusts until object is expelled or person loses consciousness.

steps.title: If Unconscious
steps.text: Lower them carefully to ground. Call emergency services immediately. Begin CPR — each time you open the airway, look for and remove any visible obstruction.

title: Anaphylaxis

steps.title: Call Emergency Services Immediately
steps.text: Call 911 NOW. Anaphylaxis is life-threatening. Do not wait to see if symptoms improve.

steps.title: Use Epinephrine Auto-Injector
steps.text: If available (EpiPen / Auvi-Q): Remove safety cap. Press firmly to outer thigh (through clothing if needed). Hold for 3 seconds. Remove. Note time.

steps.title: Position the Person
steps.text: Lay person flat with legs elevated UNLESS breathing difficulty — then have them sit upright. If unconscious and breathing, recovery position.

steps.title: Second Dose if Needed
steps.text: If symptoms persist after 5–15 minutes and a second auto-injector is available, administer a second dose.

steps.title: Monitor Breathing
steps.text: Stay with the person. If they stop breathing, begin CPR.

steps.title: Hospital Required
steps.text: All anaphylaxis patients need hospital observation — even after epinephrine. Biphasic reactions can occur hours later.

notes: Signs: hives, throat swelling, difficulty breathing, drop in blood pressure, vomiting, rapid pulse, loss of consciousness.

title: Stroke — FAST Protocol

steps.title: F — Face Drooping
steps.text: Ask them to smile. Does one side of the face droop or appear uneven?

steps.title: A — Arm Weakness
steps.text: Ask them to raise both arms. Does one arm drift downward or feel weak?

steps.title: S — Speech Difficulty
steps.text: Ask them to repeat a simple phrase. Is speech slurred, strange, or impossible?

steps.title: T — Time to Call
steps.text: If ANY of the above signs are present — call emergency services IMMEDIATELY. Note the time symptoms started.

steps.title: While Waiting
steps.text: Keep them comfortable and calm. Do NOT give food or water. Do NOT give aspirin unless directed by paramedics. Lay flat unless vomiting — then recovery position.

notes: Time is critical — every minute counts. 'Time is brain' — the sooner treatment starts, the better the outcome.

steps.title: Remove from Source
steps.text: Stop the burning. Remove the person from the heat source, or extinguish flames safely. Remove hot jewellery and clothing (unless stuck to skin).

steps.title: Cool the Burn
steps.text: Run cool (NOT cold/ice) running water over burn for 20 minutes. Do NOT use ice, butter, toothpaste, or any creams.

steps.title: Cover Loosely
steps.text: Cover with a sterile dressing, cling wrap, or clean cloth. Do NOT wrap tightly.

steps.title: Assess Severity
steps.text: Seek emergency care for: burns larger than palm size, burns on face/hands/genitals/joints, deep burns (white/charred), chemical/electrical burns, burns in children.

steps.title: Pain Relief
steps.text: OTC paracetamol or ibuprofen for pain if tolerated. Seek medical attention for all but minor burns.

steps.title: Call Emergency Services
steps.text: For severe / uncontrolled bleeding, call 911 immediately.

steps.title: Apply Direct Pressure
steps.text: Use a clean cloth, sterile pad, or bare hands if necessary. Press firmly and continuously on the wound.

steps.title: Maintain Pressure
steps.text: Do NOT remove the cloth — if it soaks through, add more on top. Continue pressing for at least 10 minutes.

steps.title: Tourniquet (limbs only)
steps.text: For severe limb bleeding not controlled by pressure: apply tourniquet 5–8 cm above wound. Tighten until bleeding stops. Note time applied. Do NOT remove.

steps.title: Position
steps.text: If possible and no spinal injury suspected, raise the injured limb above heart level.

steps.title: Protect from Injury
steps.text: Clear the area of hard/sharp objects. Cushion the head. Do NOT restrain the person.

steps.title: Position
steps.text: Gently turn them onto their side (recovery position) to prevent aspiration if vomiting occurs.

steps.title: Time the Seizure
steps.text: Note start and end time. Call emergency services if seizure lasts more than 5 minutes.

steps.title: Do NOT Put Anything in Mouth
steps.text: Never put anything in the person's mouth — this is dangerous and unnecessary.

steps.title: After the Seizure
steps.text: Keep them in recovery position. Speak calmly. They may be confused for several minutes. Stay with them.

steps.title: When to Call Emergency Services
steps.text: Call if: seizure lasts > 5 min, second seizure follows, person doesn't regain consciousness, injury occurred, first seizure ever, person is pregnant or diabetic.
